descriptionChirho: Qal intransitive sense: to go down, come down, descend, or penetrate deeper. Used in Job 21:13 (they go down to Sheol in peace), Ps 38:2 (your hand has come down upon me), Prov 17:10 (a rebuke goes deeper/penetrates into a wise man), and Jer 21:13 (who will come down against us). Arabic renders ينحدر (yanhadir 'descend') or ينزل (yanzil 'come down'), Korean uses 내려가다 (naeryeogada 'go down') and 스미다 (seumida 'soak in' for Prov 17:10), Spanish descienden/descendera/penetra. The Proverbs usage shows semantic extension from physical descent to psychological penetration.

Piel intensive sense: to press down, bend low, or cause to settle by force or weight. Found in 2 Sam 22:35 and its parallel Ps 18:34 (bending a bronze bow -- God giving strength), and Ps 65:10 (settling/flattening the furrows of the land with rain). Arabic uses تحني (tahni 'to bend'), Korean 굽히다 (gupida 'to bend') for the bow passages and 내리다 (naerida 'to bring down') for settling. Spanish renders doblado ('bent') for the bow and asentando ('settling') for the land. The Piel intensifies the base meaning from simple descent to forceful pressing down.

Niphal passive/reflexive sense: to sink in, be thrust or driven into something. In Ps 38:2, God's arrows have 'sunk into' the psalmist (נִחֲתוּ), expressing the deep penetration of divine discipline. Arabic نزلت (nazalat 'descended'), Korean 꽂혔도다 (kkojyeotdoda 'were stuck/pierced'), Spanish se clavaron ('were driven in'). The Korean and Spanish translations especially capture the passive piercing nuance distinct from the simple intransitive descent of the Qal.

Hiphil causative sense: to cause to come down, bring down, or send down from above. Found in Joel 3:11 (Joel 4:11 MT) as an imperative prayer: 'bring down your warriors, O YHWH.' Arabic أنزل (anzil 'send down'), Korean 내려보내소서 (naeryobonasoseo 'please send down'), Spanish haz descender ('cause to descend'). All translations uniformly render a causative 'send/bring down,' distinguishing this clearly from the intransitive Qal descent.

Niphal sense of being shattered or broken, expressing violent destruction rather than spatial descent. In 1 Sam 2:10 (Hannah's song), YHWH's adversaries 'will be shattered' -- a dramatic metaphor of divine judgment. Arabic ينسحقون (yansahiqun 'are crushed'), Korean 부서지다 (buseojida 'to be shattered'), Spanish seran quebrantados ('will be broken'). This sense is semantically distant from physical descent, likely a secondary development from the idea of being brought low or struck down, but the cross-linguistic evidence (crushing/shattering rather than descending) confirms a distinct lexicographic sense.
